issues.legal_issue: A reviewing court may decline to interfere with cancellation of an allotment when the authorities’ finding that the claimant lacked the qualifying interest is supported by relevant material and amounts to a finding that the allotment was obtained through false representation, even without an express finding using those words.
material_facts: The allotment was made on the basis of a claimed occupancy interest in abandoned property.
The authorities relied on land records showing that the claimants were ordinary tenants at will rather than occupancy tenants, and found that the supporting affidavits could not be relied on.
The claimants did not challenge the accuracy of the land records when responding to the cancellation notice.
The High Court dismissed the constitutional challenge to the cancellation, and the claimants appealed by special leave.
issues.conclusion: The authorities’ findings and the inference of false representation were supported by relevant material; the High Court was justified in declining to exercise its constitutional review jurisdiction, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 24(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, the Chief Settlement Commissioner could cancel the allotment; Section 33 provided for revision. An express finding of fraud or false representation was not essential where the authorities’ findings, based on relevant material, necessarily supported the inference that the allotment had been obtained by false representation. The High Court was justified in declining relief under Articles 226 and 227 where no jurisdictional error or error of law apparent on the face of the record was shown. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The claimant brought a special-leave appeal after a court dismissed a constitutional challenge to an administrative decision.
predicates.official_records_negated_qualifying_inte: The authorities relied on official records that showed the claimant did not hold the interest required to qualify for the benefit.
predicates.claimant_did_not_challenge_underlying_re: The claimant did not contest the accuracy of the official records when given an opportunity to respond to the proposed cancellation.
predicates.authorities_inferred_false_representatio: The authorities’ findings about the claimant’s lack of a qualifying interest supported an inference that the benefit had been obtained through a false representation.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal follows dismissal of a constitutional challenge, official records negate the required interest, the claimant leaves those records unchallenged, and the authorities infer false representation, the reviewing court may properly decline constitutional review.
